Package hadur2.core.move

Class StopPointSurf

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.move.StopPointSurf
public class StopPointSurf extends Object
MOVE-25: a second duel surf, built from how DrussGT and BeepBoop plan (docs/bench/surf-b-rivals-read.md). Off by default; SurfMover hands it the tick only when the duel switches it on.

What it changes, and why. The three-option surf re-rates orbit either way or stop every tick, each against a danger that is a sum of narrow kernels (one bot width) round the views' neighbours. Go-to surfing on that surface lost (-0.36 APS, 2026-10-15): with dozens of stop points, the cheapest one is mostly a gap between neighbours, a low estimate by chance. Both rivals that plan over many points smooth first: DrussGT with a Cauchy kernel about 0.12 of a guess factor wide, BeepBoop with an exponential one about 0.08 wide, each over a histogram normalised to a probability. This surf does the same on Hadur's own views (MoveController.dangerProfile(hadur2.core.model.Wave, int, int)), so the information is unchanged and only the planner differs:

  • Options. Every stop point along both orbits until the wave passes, thinned to 7 px apart, plus standing still (DrussGT's predictPositions and filterPlaceTimes).
  • Danger. The probability mass of the smoothed histogram over the precise intersection of driving to the point, counting only what our bullet shadows let through, times the bullet's damage, over sqrt(4 + t) for the ticks t until the wave breaks (BeepBoop's time weight; Hadur's 1/t made the second wave nearly weightless), times the surf's distancing factor, times DrussGT's closeness term (650 - 34) / (d - 34) at the leg's end.
  • Two waves. The cheapest first-wave points, in order, get the second wave's cheapest stop point from where they leave us added, with pruning once a first-wave danger alone is not below the best total.
  • Commitment. The point is kept until the waves surfed change, their bullet shadows are recomputed, the views learn a hit or a visit, or we are more than 2.0 px off the predicted path (DrussGT replans only when its stats change).

Angles are radians on Robocode's compass; distances in px; times in ticks.
